title: Jet minors, local level topology and the reachable diagram bound
statement:
Let $X$ be a reduced finite-type $\mathbf Q$-scheme locally closed in a smooth $\mathbf Q$-scheme $Z$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Write $H_X(x)=\Lambda^{\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbf Q}\kappa(x)}h_x$, where $h_x(q)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,x}/\mathfrak m_x^{q+1})$ and $\Lambda f(q)=\sum_{i=0}^qf(i)$, with lexicographic order [def-trf-hilbert-samuel-invariant]. These lengths are finite. For any affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$, set $J=\ker(R\otimes_{\mathbf Q}R\to R)$ and $P^q=(R\otimes_{\mathbf Q}R)/J^{q+1}$, as an $R$-module through the first factor [def-trf-diagonal-jets]. Each $P^q$ admits a finite presentation $R^{u_q}\xrightarrow{A_q}R^{v_q}\to P^q\to0$ and, for $1\le c\le v_q$, the locus $H_X(x)(q)\ge c$ is the vanishing locus of all $(v_q-c+1)$-minors of $A_q$ (the locus is all points if $c\le0$ and empty if $c>v_q$).
At every $a\in X$ there are an affine neighbourhood $U$, a finite set $F\subset\mathbf N^{\mathbf N}$, and $q_0\ge0$ such that $H_X(U)\subset F$, distinct members of $F$ first differ at an index at most $q_0$, and $\{x\in U:H_X(x)(q)\le H_X(a)(q)\text{ for all }q\le q_0\}$ is an open neighbourhood of $a$ on which $H_X(x)\le_{\rm lex}H_X(a)$. In particular every lexicographic upper-level set is closed.
Fix a finite smooth ambient chart cover near $X$ with at most $d$ coordinates on every chart. Let $\mathcal R_X$ be all values $H_{X'}(x')$ after arbitrary finite histories of smooth-center ambient blowups and scheme-theoretic strict transforms of $X$ [def-nagata-global-blowup] [def-nagata-strict-transform], with each center contained in the current $X'$ and locally $H$-constant. Then every value in $\mathcal R_X$ is the monomial-complement counting function of a Taylor diagram in at most $d$ variables; the ambient charts remain smooth and their reduced strict transforms are reduced. There is no sequence $v_i\in\mathcal R_X$ with $v_{i+1}<_{\rm lex}v_i$ for every $i$. The assertion includes zero blowups, histories of different lengths and subsequences separated by arbitrarily long plateaus.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, pp.93--94; BM 1997 Remarks 9.1, Theorem 9.2, Lemma 9.3 and Corollary 3.20; BMT 6.1. Determinantal and fixed-dimension assembly from old proof steps 1,2,9. No Stacks tag states this package.

proof.text: The field $\mathbf Q$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q$. Since $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q$ is locally of finite type, [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] with $V=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q$ shows that every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$ has $R$ a finitely generated $\mathbf Q$-algebra, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $R$ Noetherian. Stalks are localizations of Noetherian rings: an ideal in a localization is generated by the images of generators of its contraction. For $B=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, the cyclic nonzero module $B/\mathfrak m_x^{q+1}$ is supported only at $\mathfrak m_x$: at a different prime choose an element of $\mathfrak m_x$ outside that prime, whose $(q+1)$st power annihilates the quotient and becomes a unit. Thus [lem-sc-generic-stalk-finite-length] gives the asserted finite lengths. For every affine $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$, [lem-trf-jet-diagram-hilbert-control] gives finiteness of $P^q$ and identifies its fibre dimension with $H_X(x)(q)$, including nonclosed points. By [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-module-finite-presentation] it has the stated finite presentation.

source.place: Tags 01T6 (morphisms.tex lemma-finite-type-noetherian), 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 00FP (lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation), 00L5 (lemma-support-point); jet identification from BM Remarks 9.1 / existing jet-diagram node

proof.text: Tensor this presentation with $L=\kappa(x)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], its cokernel is $P^q\otimes_R L$, so $H_X(x)(q)=v_q-\operatorname{rank}_L A_q(x)$. For $s=v_q-c+1>0$, rank at least $s$ is equivalent to a nonzero $s$-minor. Indeed a nonzero minor makes its $s$ columns independent. Conversely choose $s$ independent columns; their map $L^s\to L^{v_q}$ is injective, so [lem-weil-pbc-field-injective-matrix-nonzero-maximal-minor] supplies $s$ rows with nonzero determinant. Thus $H_X(x)(q)\ge c$ is equivalent to every $s$-minor vanishing in $L$, or to their belonging to the prime of $x$. This is precisely their closed zero locus. If $s$ exceeds the number of columns, all such minors vanish and rank is automatically below $s$. The cokernel dimension lies between zero and $v_q$, giving the two endpoint conventions. Taking complements shows that each coordinate sublevel $H_X(x)(q)\le b$ is open.

source.place: Tag 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact); elementary rank/minor calculation, with field injective-minor lemma (00MY/00MW) as cited

proof.text: Work locally where $X$ is closed in an affine smooth ambient chart. Such etale coordinate charts exist by applying [lem-trf-smooth-pair-blowup-local-models] to the identity closed immersion of that smooth affine scheme into itself; only its coordinate assertion is used. On a sufficiently small such chart [lem-trf-jet-diagram-hilbert-control] gives finitely many Taylor diagrams, and its dimension identities identify their counting functions with $H_X$. Consequently $H_X$ has finite image locally. The chart restrictions cover $X$, and the jet identities commute with etale localization by the same cited statement. Shrink to an affine neighbourhood $U$ of $a$ inside one such neighbourhood, and take $F=H_X(U)$, a finite set. This argument does not assume that $a$ is closed.

source.place: BM 1997 Remarks 9.1, Theorem 9.2 and Lemma 9.3 (jet-diagram input); Stacks 0FUE, lemma-etale-local-structure for coordinates

proof.text: For each unequal pair $f,g\in F$, take its first differing degree. Choose $q_0$ at least all these finitely many degrees, taking $q_0=0$ when there are no unequal pairs. Then the finite intersection $V=\bigcap_{q\le q_0}\{x\in U:H_X(x)(q)\le H_X(a)(q)\}$ is open by step 2 and contains $a$. If $H_X(x)\ne H_X(a)$ for $x\in V$, their first differing degree is at most $q_0$ by the choice of $F,q_0$; at that degree the imposed inequality is strict. Hence $H_X(x)<_{\rm lex}H_X(a)$. Equality gives the remaining case. For any threshold sequence $v$, each point $a$ with $H_X(a)<_{\rm lex}v$ therefore has an open neighbourhood contained in that strict sublevel. Their union is the complement of $\{x:H_X(x)\ge_{\rm lex}v\}$, proving closedness of every upper-level set.

source.place: Finite first-difference argument assembling steps 2--3; no external lemma

proof.text: Track each initial affine ambient coordinate chart separately, with $e\le d$ coordinates. Induct on the length of a history restricted over this chart. Length zero is the given smooth ambient and reduced $X$. For the induction step, localize the current ambient to affine opens, so it is separated and of finite type; the smooth closed center restricts to a smooth closed subscheme. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-center-blowup-geometry] there. Its conclusion gives smooth finite-type ambient blowups and reduced scheme-theoretic strict transforms of the reduced closed $X$. These restrictions compute the global ones: for an open immersion $W\subset P$ (flat, and every component of $X\cap W$ has the generic point of a component of $X$), [lem-trf-strict-transform-flat-etale-base-change] identifies $P^+\times_PW$ with $\operatorname{Bl}_{C\cap W}(W)$ and the restricted strict transform with that of $X\cap W$. Smoothness and reducedness being local, they cover the whole transform. Locally closed $X$ is first made closed by an ambient restriction. This proves the two geometric assertions for every finite length, also when a center is empty or removes a whole open component.

source.place: Stacks 0FUT, more-morphisms.tex lemma-blowup; reduced strict transforms in the cited smooth-center geometry statement

proof.text: The coordinate bound also propagates at each induction step. By [lem-trf-smooth-pair-blowup-local-models], near a center point the blowup is an etale pullback of the blowup of $(y_1,\ldots,y_b)$ in $\mathbf A^{a+b}_{\mathbf Q}$. By [lem-trf-coordinate-subspace-blowup-charts] its nonempty charts have exactly $a+b$ coordinates: $a$ old $x$ coordinates, $y_i$, and $b-1$ ratios. If $b=0$ the blowup there is empty. Off the center the blowup is unchanged: on $W=P\setminus C$ the extended ideal is the unit ideal, whose blowup is $W$, and [lem-trf-strict-transform-flat-etale-base-change] identifies the restriction of the blowup with it. The starting coordinate chart is smooth of relative dimension $e$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth] and [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence]. The same two statements show that a nonempty etale coordinate-subspace model has relative dimension $a+b$ and its blowup charts retain that dimension. Thus on each nonempty overlap $a+b=e$, since both numbers are the fibre dimension at a point. Induction retains $e\le d$ everywhere above this initial chart; no new variable is added by the ratios. Applying [lem-trf-jet-diagram-hilbert-control] to the reduced closed strict transform on each resulting etale chart expresses every reachable $H_{X'}(x')$ as a Taylor-diagram counting function in $e\le d$ variables.

source.place: Stacks 0FUE (lemma-etale-local-structure), 0H1H (remark-relative-blowup), 01VA/02NL relative dimension; BM Corollary 3.20 via jet-diagram control

proof.text: Put all these diagrams in one fixed $d$-variable set. For an upward-closed diagram $D\subset\mathbf N^e$, define $\widetilde D\subset\mathbf N^d$ to consist of exponents whose first $e$ coordinates lie in $D$ or whose last $d-e$ coordinates are not all zero. It is upward closed. Its complement consists exactly of $(\alpha,0)$ with $\alpha\notin D$, with unchanged total degree, so its counting function is exactly that of $D$. This padding uses extra variables in the ideal, rather than adjoining free quotient variables. An infinite strict descent of values anywhere in $\mathcal R_X$ would therefore give an infinite strict descent of counting functions of upward-closed diagrams in $d$ variables, contrary to [lem-trf-jet-diagram-hilbert-control]. The argument selects a diagram for each value separately and never compares consecutive histories; hence zero blowups, unrelated history lengths, and arbitrary intervening plateaus are all covered.

source.place: BM Corollary 3.20, fixed-dimension counting-function DCC as stated by jet-diagram control; explicit padding argument
